boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fort Wagner II record (July 18-September 7, 1863) in Operations Against the Defenses of Charleston [April-September 1863]. The frozen interval runs from the second assault through the siege to the evacuation of Wagner. The bombardments of Fort Sumter (SC008) and the September 8 boat attack (SC009) are separate records; their losses are not added here. Campaign-wide marches, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text and the live page read 6,800 total (US 5,000; CS 1,800). Jones gives Wagner's garrison on July 18 as an aggregate of about seventeen hundred, the Union force about seven thousand when Beauregard weighed a counterattack, and the Fifty-fourth Massachusetts as nearly a thousand; Gillmore calls the assaulting regiments all small. For the siege Jones gives Union returns of 29,405 present (4661 sick) in August and 28,981 (5269 sick) in September, and about 900 Confederates and 9,000 Union soldiers on the island on September 6; Keitt wrote that he had fewer than four hundred effective infantry. In August Gillmore wrote that Beauregard had twice as many men and five times the artillery.
claims.rationale: Figures for different dates and scopes in a record spanning fifty-two days; the frozen figures' basis is not stated in any inspected passage. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: Gillmore established counter-batteries to dismount Wagner's guns and open the way to an assault; after July 18 he gave priority to demolishing Sumter from ground already held and pressed Wagner by regular approaches. Jones says Gillmore declined another assault unless the navy furnished a column, and that Wagner was finally to be taken by sap and storm.
claims.rationale: Stated plans from an interested report and a history.

claims.value: Gillmore chose twilight for the assault and says Seymour commanded the column. Jones reports Seymour's charge that Putnam refused to advance, citing Gillmore's orders, and that Stevenson did not obey an order to support; Seymour blamed the delay. Jones names Taliaferro, then Hagood and Keitt, as Confederate commanders in Wagner, and Beauregard as deciding the evacuation after a council. The frozen commanders are Major General Quincy Gillmore (US) and General P. G. T. Beauregard (CS).
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report and a history; the Seymour-Putnam dispute is preserved, and no listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Gillmore says the southeast bastion was held nearly three hours on July 18 and then given up, and that when the Confederates evacuated on the night of September 6-7 nearly all escaped. Jones calls the July 18 repulse complete and disastrous and the September occupation a barren victory.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The frozen interval ends with the Union occupation of Wagner; the result is preserved as frozen.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,689 total (US 1,515; CS 174); the live field reads 1737 (US 1515; CS 222). Jones gives the Confederate loss on July 18 as 174 and says the Federal loss was never officially ascertained, citing Taliaferro's estimate of not less than 2000 and Beauregard's 3000; elsewhere he gives 1600 to 3000. For the whole fifty-eight days on the island he gives 641 Confederate killed and wounded. At the evacuation Gillmore says seventy men were intercepted; Jones says two boats' crews and twenty-seven soldiers.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. July 18, siege-wide and evacuation figures are different populations and must not be added to one another or to SC005.

open_questions: Seymour's, Putnam's, Stevenson's, Terry's and the engineers' reports, Beauregard's general report, Taliaferro's, Hagood's and Keitt's reports, and the Union and Confederate casualty returns for July 18 and the siege remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (NPS battle page and frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Quincy A. Gillmore's report dated February 28, 1864 (Official Records I, XXVIII part 1, No. 2) is one family of interested Union accounts. Samuel Jones's The Siege of Charleston (1911) is a posthumous Confederate general's history that quotes Gillmore's, Seymour's, Strong's, Ripley's, Taliaferro's and Beauregard's reports and is not independent of them. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
